No test verifies that null videoPath flows through correctly when a movie has no file on disk. The null path is safe by interface contract (IBookmarkSettingsService.ShowAsync accepts string? videoPath = null) but an explicit null-path test would add defence-in-depth.

comments.note: The AddBookmark call site now uses both optional args as named arguments: videoPath: _videoPath, ct: linked.Token. This is an improvement over the WP-001 pattern (which only named ct:) — both optional parameters are now self-documenting at the call site. No ambiguity about which positional slot each value occupies.

MakeSut factory correctly forwards videoPath as a named argument. All pre-existing tests pass videoPath = null (defaulted) and are unaffected. The new AddBookmarkCommand_PassesVideoPath_ToSettingsService test is clean, focused, and correctly leverages FakeBookmarkSettingsService.LastVideoPath from WP-001.

EditBookmarkCommand still omits videoPath from ShowAsync (falls back to null default). This was logged by Developer and QA as out-of-WP-002 scope. The null fallback is safe by interface contract. Recommend a follow-up WP for Edit-mode frame-capture support.
